diagnostic_evidence.quote: It has been proven in \cite{pan2024block} that any circulant quaternion matrix is fast block diagonalizable by means of fast Fourier transforms (FFTs), with each eigen-block being of size at most $2\times 2$.
Then, it is easy to see that $\matcomplexify{c(T_n)}$ is unitarily similar to the following $2n$-by-$2n$ matrix

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's Fourier construction gives small blocks, not direct diagonalization of the quaternion matrix by F_{p,n}. For example, take n=5 and Strang first column (5,j,k,-k,-j). This is an HPD Hermitian circulant. If any single-axis quaternion Fourier matrix diagonalized it, its diagonal would be real, so reconstructing the matrix would put every entry in the same complex slice R+Ru. Its j and k entries make that impossible.

failure_location.quote:
We show that Strang's circulant preconditioners can be diagionalized by 
discrete quaternion Fourier transform matrices 
whereas general quaternion circulant matrices cannot be diagonalized by them.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace direct Fourier diagonalization by Fourier block diagonalization, followed, when actual diagonalization is needed, by diagonalization of the small Hermitian blocks.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised distinction between Strang circulants and general quaternion circulants is false. The block-FFT implementation and its operation count do not require this stronger claim.
issues.title: Quaternion Fourier matrices do not generally diagonalize Strang preconditioners
issues.why_classification: This changes a substantive advertised structural conclusion, but the source-supported small-block reduction preserves the computational scope and O(n log n) cost.

issues.failure_explanation: Every polynomial in the displayed class has equal endpoint values at -pi and pi, and every uniform limit retains that property. Thus this class is not dense in all continuous functions on the closed interval; h(x)=x is a counterexample. The claimed passage from Fourier moments to testing against every continuous h consequently uses a false premise.

failure_location.quote: is dense in $C([-\pi,\pi])$, where $C([-\pi,\pi])$ denotes the set of all $\mathbb{Q}_{(0,1)}$-valued continuous functions defined on $[-\pi,\pi]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use density in the periodic continuous functions, which include continuous tests supported inside the interval, or apply Fourier uniqueness. First obtain the negative Fourier moments by conjugating the already established identities.
issues.overall_effect: The written proof of the real-valuedness of phi_1(f), and arguments relying on that proof, have a gap; the structural conclusion itself can be retained.
issues.title: The generating-function proof invokes a false uniform-density assertion
issues.why_classification: A standard local Fourier-uniqueness argument repairs the proof without changing any substantive result or hypothesis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $G[f](x)$ is a 2-by-2 Hermitian matrix for each $x\in[-\pi,\pi]$,

issues.failure_explanation: The off-diagonal entries -b and conjugate(b) are not Hermitian partners unless b=0. For the admissible generating function f(x)=2+sin(x)q, the declared G is [[2,-sin(x)],[sin(x),2]], with nonreal eigenvalues 2±p sin(x), rather than the claimed real branches 2±|sin(x)|. The quadratic-form identity also requires the plus-sign upper-right entry. This erroneous sign is used again in the circulant Fourier-block calculation, not merely in an isolated display.

failure_location.quote: It is clear that $G[f](x)$ is Hermitian for each $x$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use G[f](x)=[[phi_1(f)(x),phi_2(f)(x)],[conjugate(phi_2(f)(x)),phi_1(f)(-x)]], as the quadratic-form expansion itself produces, and correct the corresponding off-diagonal Fourier-block identifications consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The stated integral representation, identification of the eigenvalue branches, and applications of Hermitian spectral results to the declared G are invalid as written.
issues.title: The declared block symbol is not Hermitian
issues.why_classification: The source already contains the correct plus-sign quadratic-form matrix. Consistent local corrections preserve the stated eigenvalue bounds, distribution formulas, and convergence rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The lag in E[x(t-s') conjugate(x(t-s))] is s-s', not s'-s. Consequently the lower-triangular entries of the normal-equation matrix must be conjugate(eta(s'-s)), whereas the paper puts eta(s'-s) there and retains the original coefficient ordering and right-hand side. The resulting system does not generally compute the minimizer of the stated prediction objective.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use matrix entries eta(s-s'), or retain the printed Toeplitz matrix and reverse both the coefficient vector and the right-hand side. Propagate the convention to the sampled system and correct the interpretation or computation of the prediction experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The population and sampled systems are not the claimed prediction normal equations. Their Hermitian Toeplitz spectral properties can still hold, but solving them does not establish the advertised prediction coefficients.
issues.title: The prediction system reverses the covariance lag
issues.why_classification: A reversal preserves the spectral theory, but the application computes a different input-output map. Repairing the population and sampled predictors also requires revising what the reported solves demonstrate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\beta$ is a given quaternion parameter with $|\beta|\in(0,1)$;

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis permits real beta, for example beta=1/2. Then beta_I=0, so m and the subsequent ratios involving |beta_I| are undefined. Thus the displayed generating-function construction does not cover all parameters admitted by the example.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat beta_I=0 separately: phi_2(f)=0 and phi_1(f)(theta)=4 delta^2/(1+beta^2-2 beta cos(theta)). Use the current polar formulas only when beta_I is nonzero.
issues.overall_effect: The polar-coordinate derivation and explicit generating-function formulas omit the real-parameter case.
issues.title: The AR(1) formulas are undefined for permitted real parameters
issues.why_classification: A routine scalar special case restores the full stated parameter range without altering the method or positivity guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: For n=2m the defined preconditioner discards the lag-m coefficient, but the asserted spectral formula includes it through f_m. For example, f(x)=3+2 cos(x) and n=2 give c(T_2)=3I, while the formula samples f_1 at 0 and pi and predicts eigenvalues 5 and 1. This failure is independent of the quaternion-symbol sign issue.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use truncation order floor((n-1)/2), while keeping floor(n/2) as the endpoint of the frequency-index range. Then repeat the uniform-convergence argument with that truncation.
issues.overall_effect: The exact finite-dimensional spectral formula is false for even n, and the subsequent limit proof invokes that false formula.
issues.title: The circulant spectrum uses the wrong truncation for even dimensions
issues.why_classification: This local parity correction preserves the defined preconditioner, all dimensions, and the asymptotic spectral and convergence conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: Even after correcting the off-diagonal sign, the simultaneous Fourier reduction has lower-right entry phi_1(f_m)(-theta), not conjugate(phi_1(f_m)(theta))=phi_1(f_m)(theta). These need not agree. For a(theta)=5+2 sin(theta) and b(theta)=sin(theta), the correct block has eigenvalues 5±sqrt(5)|sin(theta)|, whereas the printed diagonal pairing gives 5+2 sin(theta)±|sin(theta)|. The subsequent frequency-pair similarities likewise substitute conjugation for reflection; oddness of b does not imply b is purely imaginary.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Derive each Fourier block from its coefficients, retaining the reflected argument in the lower-right entry. Fold opposite frequencies using the evenness of the explicitly given check-f and hat-f eigenvalue branches instead of the incorrect conjugation identities.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed block unitary similarity and the proof reducing the frequency range are unsupported even after repairing the separate sign and even-dimension defects.
issues.title: The circulant proof confuses conjugation with frequency reflection
issues.why_classification: Correct Fourier bookkeeping and a short use of the existing eigenvalue formulas repair the argument without changing its conclusions or complexity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The PCG solver using an HPD preconditioner $P\in\mathbb{Q}^{n\times n}$

issues.failure_explanation: The Gram argument establishes HPD of tilde-H, not of its Strang preconditioner. Take n=4, M=5 and real samples (1,-1,1,-1,1). The displayed sample construction has full column rank, so tilde-H is HPD. But tilde-eta(0)=1 and tilde-eta(1)=-4/5, giving Strang first column (1,-4/5,0,-4/5); its all-ones eigenvector has eigenvalue -3/5. Thus the proposed application violates PCG's stated HPD-preconditioner hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: Hence, if $\tilde{T}$ is a full rank matrix, then $\tilde{H}$ is an HPD quaternion matrix. One can then apply the PCG  solver with the circulant preconditioner to solve the linear system \eqref{apphermqtsystem}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Check that the sampled Strang preconditioner is HPD before using PCG with it. If it is not, use the already discussed unpreconditioned CG method or another verified HPD preconditioner, and limit Strang-specific guarantees accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The sampled-system procedure is not justified for all full-rank sample matrices. Population asymptotic positivity does not supply a finite-sample positivity guarantee.
issues.title: Positive definiteness of the sampled matrix does not justify Strang-PCG
issues.why_classification: A local safeguard or alternative preconditioner suffices for solvability, but the unconditional recommendation of Strang-PCG for these sampled systems must be weakened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We call a triple of pure quaternions $(\unitp,\unitq,\unitr)$ orthonormal if and only if  $\unitp,\unitq,\unitr$ are all units and any two of them are orthogonal.

issues.failure_explanation: Orthonormality permits both orientations. The triple (i,j,-k) satisfies the definition, but pq=k=-r, contradicting part (i). The same omitted condition affects the body: for this triple, taking A=r makes the asserted decomposition produce pq=-r rather than A. Hence the specified phi_2 and complexification formulas are not valid for every allowed triple.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose orthogonal unit p and q and require r=pq throughout, or explicitly restrict the triples to positively oriented orthonormal triples.
issues.overall_effect: The Hamilton multiplication rules and proofs using the stated complex representation lack a necessary basis-orientation hypothesis.
issues.title: Orthonormal quaternion axes need an orientation hypothesis
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local basis convention. It excludes no quaternion matrices or generating functions and preserves all substantive spectral and algorithmic scope.
